# #3065: Patch: `cargo jackioh run-sim` plays whole dungeon runs with the AI in the player's seat and reports how each kind of fight goes
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The dungeon run's numbers, such as enemy health, prices and what a boss pays out, are placeholders. No test or tool has ever played one of its fights to the end: today's checks start each fight and then make up its result. Once this is built, the maintainer runs one command that plays seeded runs from start to finish with the AI in the player's seat. It prints a table: how often each kind of fight is won, how much health it costs, how far a run gets and what it scores. That gives the placeholders something to be tuned against.

## Why

- `spec/15-dungeon-run.md:286` and `docs/dungeon-run.md:236` list tuning the strawmen as open: `RUN_LEVEL_EMBERS` (`crates/run/src/config.rs:73`), `RUN_ENEMY_HEALTH` (:90) and the `RUN_SCORE_*` weights (:186-208).
- `crates/run/src/walk_tests.rs:58-66`: every fight result is made up ("`fight_won` clamps HP, so any won report is accepted"). `check_fight` (:256-260) creates and begins a fight's game but never plays it.
- `crates/ai/src/match_.rs:69-79`: `MatchSetup` has `dealt`, `last_boards` and `glitch_boards` but no deck marks, so `play_match` cannot play a run fight's Radiant and buffed cards. `ReplayInput` already has them (`crates/engine/src/replay.rs:808`).
- No file in `crates/tools/src` names a deck mark, so the fuzz never plays a game with one either.

## Proposal

- `MatchSetup` takes optional `deck_marks`, passed through `play_match` and the fold. Without them, every game is created and folded as today.
- A new `cargo jackioh run-sim --seeds N [--skill …] [--budget …]` in `crates/tools`, which gains `jackioh-run` as a dependency:
  - each fight comes from `run_fight_setup`, and each result goes back through `run_fight_report`;
  - the player's seat is the AI at R747000's skill knob;
  - map, pack, shop and event choices follow a simple seeded policy, like the walk tests'.
- It prints win rate and HP lost by node kind, HP at each boss, rows reached, turns per fight, score and Embers.
- A per-PR test at a tiny budget, a daily `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` sweep, the tools README row, and `scripts/ci-scope.sh`'s map if the new dependency needs it.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/match_.rs` and `crates/ai/tests/ai/match_setup.rs`.
- A new `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`, plus `crates/tools/src/main.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and `README.md`.
- Possibly `scripts/ci-scope.sh`.
- §15.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A marked card in a `MatchSetup` starts Radiant and buffed, and its record folds to its hash. A setup without marks folds every existing record unchanged.
- [ ] A per-PR tools test plays one seed's first fights at a tiny budget. Every fight ends cleanly (no refusal, fallback or search panic) and folds to its hash, and the run file folds to the same end.
- [ ] The daily sweep plays N seeds at full budget and prints the report.
- [ ] `crates/tools/README.md`'s command table lists the command, so the acceptance README check passes.
- [ ] No strawman number changes in this pull request.

## Size and risks

About 6 to 8 files and 500 lines. Label it hard, since it spans crates. AI-against-AI games are slow, so the per-PR test stays tiny and the full sweep runs daily. The AI plays the player's seat better or worse than a person would, so the report is broken down by skill and is a guide, not a target.

## Goal

`cargo jackioh run-sim --seeds N [--from K] [--skill S,…] [--budget tiny|full]` plays seeded whole dungeon runs on the catalog's content:

- Each fight is set up by `run_fight_setup`, played by `play_match` and reported through `run_fight_report`.
- The player (P1) is the AI at R747000's skill; the enemy is the AI at full skill.
- Every other choice follows a seeded policy.

For each skill it prints, by kind of fight, the win rate, HP lost and turns. It also prints HP at each boss, rows reached, runs won, score and Embers.

6. **`crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`.**

   - that it is a guide for tuning (§15.13), not a target;
   - that the policy has its own stream, so the log `run_fold`s;

   End it with a block of example commands.

   **Imports.**
   - Names come from the crate roots of `jackioh_ai`, `jackioh_engine` and `jackioh_run`.
   - The exceptions are `jackioh_engine::config::PERCENT` and `jackioh_run::config::{RUN_ACT_FIGHTS, RUN_STARTER_CARDS, RUN_STARTER_SIZE}`.

   - `HEAL_BELOW_PERCENT: i32 = 60`
   - `PR_FIGHTS: usize = 3`
   - `DAILY_SEEDS: u32 = 4`
   - `DAILY_SKILLS: [f64; 2] = [AI_SKILL_MAX, 0.5]`
   - `KINDS: [RunNodeKind; 5] = [Fight, Elite, Ghost, MiniBoss, Boss]`
   - `BOSSES: usize = RUN_ACT_FIGHTS.len()`

   **`#[derive(clap::Args, Debug)] pub struct Args`.**
   - `#[arg(long)] seeds: u32`
   - `#[arg(long, default_value_t = 0)] from: u32`
   - `#[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',', value_parser = parse_skill)] skill: Vec<f64>`. An empty list means `[AI_SKILL_MAX]`.
   - `#[arg(long, value_parser = ["tiny", "full"], default_value = "full")] budget: String`
   - `parse_skill(&str) -> Result<f64, String>` refuses any value outside `AI_SKILL_MIN..=AI_SKILL_MAX`, NaN included, as `arena.rs::check_skill` does.
   - `budget_of(&str) -> SearchBudget` returns `TINY_BUDGET` for `"tiny"` and `AI_BUDGET` otherwise.

   **`fn fight_config(setup: &RunFightSetup, skill: f64, budget: SearchBudget) -> MatchConfig`.** It builds:
   - `seed`: the setup's seed.
   - `decks`: `(human_deck, enemy_deck)`.
   - `handicaps`: both seats' handicaps.
   - `controllers`: `PerPlayer::new(Ai { budget: Some(budget), skill: Some(skill) }, Ai { budget: Some(budget), skill: None })`.
   - `max_actions`: `None`.
   - `setup`: `MatchSetup { deck_marks: Some(PerPlayerOpt { p1: Some(human_marks.clone()), p2: None }), ..MatchSetup::default() }`. An empty list stores nothing (R2702000).

   **`fn play_fight(state: &RunState, content: &RunContent, skill: f64, budget: SearchBudget) -> Result<RunAction, String>`.**
   1. Call `run_fight_setup` (`None` is an `Err`), then `fight_config`.
   2. Call `validate_setup(&CreateGameOptions { seed, decks, handicaps, deck_marks, ..Default::default() }, registered_catalog(), &CardDefs::default(), SetupKind::New)` with the config's fields. On error, return `Err("the engine refuses the setup: …")`. This comes first because `create_game` panics outside `catch_unwind`.
   3. Call `play_match(&config, &mut MatchHooks::default())`.
   4. Return an `Err` naming the first of these that holds:
      - `thrown` is not empty;
      - `rejected` is not empty;
      - `fallbacks > 0`;
      - `sim_panics > 0` (include `first_sim_panic`);
      - `result` is `None`.
   5. Set `game = config.fold_args(record.log.clone())`. Return `Err` if `fold(&game)` has errors or its `hash_state` differs from `record.hash`.
   6. Return `run_fight_report(&game, PlayerId::P1)`.

   **`fn choose(state: &RunState, content: &RunContent, rng: &mut Rng) -> Result<(RunAction, RunState), String>`.**
   - It returns the first candidate that `run_reduce` accepts, with its next state.
   - If none is accepted, it returns an `Err` naming the phase and the last refusal.
   - A random index is `rng.int(len as i32) as usize`. `Rng::int(0)` is 0, so no helper is needed.

   The candidates, in order:
   - `Map`: `Go { col }` at a random column of row `state.row.map_or(0, |r| r + 1)`, then `Go { col: 0 }`.
   - `Reward` with an artifact: `TakeArtifact { take: true }`, then `false`.
   - `Reward`: `OpenPack` at a random index, then at 0.
   - `Pack { cards, keep }`: `Keep` with the first `keep` of `rng.shuffle(cards)`, then `cards[..keep]`.
   - `ExtractCard` and `ExtractArtifact`: `Extract { index: None }`.
   - `Shop { stock }`: in order,
     - `Buy` of each unsold index, in `rng.shuffle` order;
     - `MakeRadiant` at a random card;
     - `Buff` at a random card;
     - `Leave`.
   - `Campfire`: in order,
     - `Heal` when `hp * PERCENT < run_max_hp * HEAL_BELOW_PERCENT`;
     - `MakeRadiant` at a random card;
     - `Buff` at a random card;
     - `Heal`.
   - `Event { id }`: `Choose` at a random option, then the last option with no negative `hp`, `coins` or `tickets` (as in `walk_tests.rs::free_action`).
   - `Shrine { offers }`: `Bless { Some(random) }`, then `Bless { None }`.
   - `Fight`, `Won` and `Dead`: an `Err`, never `unreachable!`.

   This corrects the first plan: in a shop, `Buy`, `MakeRadiant` and `Buff` keep the run in the shop. Each one spends currency, so `Leave` always ends it.

   **Outcome types.**
   - `struct FightRow { kind: RunNodeKind, hp_before: i32, hp_after: i32, won: bool, turns: i32 }`
   - `struct RunOutcome { file: RunFile, end: RunState, fights: Vec<FightRow>, faults: Vec<String> }`

   **`fn run_setup(n: u32) -> (RunSetup, RunUnlocks)`.**
   - Seed: `run_seed(&format!("run-sim-{n}"))`.
   - Starter: `RUN_STARTER_CARDS[..RUN_STARTER_SIZE]` as `String`s.
   - No artifacts or curses.
   - `RunUnlocks::default()`.

   **`fn play_run(n: u32, content: &RunContent, fight: &dyn Fn(&RunState) -> Result<RunAction, String>, max_fights: Option<usize>) -> Result<RunOutcome, String>`.**
   1. It returns `Err` only when `run_create` refuses. The policy stream is `Rng::new(&format!("run-sim-policy-{n}"), 0)`.
   2. Loop until the phase is `Won` or `Dead`. Stop early after `max_fights` fights, or with a fault after `MAX_STEPS` steps.
      - In `Fight`: call `fight(&state)`, then `run_reduce`. Push a `FightRow` with `kind` from `run_node`, HP before and after, `won` unless the next phase is `Dead`, and the `turns` from `FightOver`.
      - In any other phase: call `choose`.
      - Log the action. On an `Err`, push `format!("run {n} ({seed}) row {:?}: {e}", state.row)` as a fault and stop. A lost fight is data, never a fault.
   3. If there are no faults, `run_fold(&file, content)` must equal the end state; otherwise push a fault.

   **Tally.**
   - `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] struct KindTally { fights: usize, won: usize, hp_lost: i64, turns: i64 }`
   - `#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)] struct Tally { runs: usize, runs_won: usize, kinds: [KindTally; KINDS.len()], boss_hp: [(i64, usize); BOSSES], rows: Vec<usize>, map_rows: usize, scores: Vec<i64> }`
   - `fn tally(outcomes: &[RunOutcome], content: &RunContent) -> Tally` fills it this way:
     - each `FightRow` adds to its kind, with `hp_lost += hp_before − hp_after`;
     - a run's k-th `is_boss()` fight adds `(hp_before, 1)` to `boss_hp[k]`;
     - `rows` takes `end.row.map_or(0, |r| r + 1)`;
     - `map_rows` is the largest `end.map.len()`;
     - `scores` takes `run_score(&end, content)`;
     - `runs_won` counts the runs that end `Won`.
   - `fn mean(sum: i64, n: usize) -> String` returns `-` when `n` is 0, otherwise `{:.1}`.
   - `Tally::render(&self, header: &str) -> String` prints, in order:
     - the header;
     - a `kind fights won win % HP lost turns` table, one `{:<10}{:>8}{:>6}{:>7}{:>9}{:>7}` row per kind (`fight`, `elite`, `ghost`, `miniBoss`, `boss`), where win % is `mean(won × PERCENT, fights)`;
     - a note that HP lost is HP entering minus HP leaving, so a lost fight loses all of it;
     - each `HP entering boss k`, with its mean and n;
     - the rows reached, as a mean and a max, out of `map_rows`;
     - runs won;
     - score and Embers (`run_embers`), each as a mean and a max.

     An empty max prints `-`.

   **`fn sweep(seeds: u32, from: u32, skills: &[f64], budget: &str, content: &RunContent) -> (String, Vec<String>)`.**
   - For each skill, run `(from..from.saturating_add(seeds)).into_par_iter().map(|n| play_run(n, content, &|s| play_fight(s, content, skill, budget_of(budget)), None)).collect::<Vec<_>>()`. Collecting keeps seed order.
   - Each table's header is `run-sim: {seeds} runs from {from}, budget {budget}, skill {skill}`.
   - Every fault, including an `Err` from `play_run`, gets ` (again: cargo jackioh run-sim --from {n} --seeds 1 --skill {skill} --budget {budget})` appended.

   **`pub fn run(args: Args) -> anyhow::Result<()>`.**
   1. Call `jackioh_cards::register_all()`.
   2. Build `run_catalog_content(registered_catalog(), &[])`.
   3. Run `sweep` and print the result.
   4. `bail!` if there is any fault.

   **`fn choose(state: &RunState, content: &RunContent, rng: &mut Rng) -> Result<(RunAction, RunState), String>`.**
   - It returns the first candidate that `run_reduce` accepts, with its next state.
   - If none is accepted, it returns an `Err` naming the phase and the last refusal.
   - A random index is `rng.int(len as i32) as usize`. `Rng::int(0)` is 0, so no helper is needed.

   The candidates, in order:
   - `Map`: `Go { col }` at a random column of row `state.row.map_or(0, |r| r + 1)`, then `Go { col: 0 }`.
   - `Reward` with an artifact: `TakeArtifact { take: true }`, then `false`.
   - `Reward`: `OpenPack` at a random index, then at 0.
   - `Pack { cards, keep }`: `Keep` with the first `keep` of `rng.shuffle(cards)`, then `cards[..keep]`.
   - `ExtractCard` and `ExtractArtifact`: `Extract { index: None }`.
   - `Shop { stock }`: in order,
     - `Buy` of each unsold index, in `rng.shuffle` order;
     - `MakeRadiant` at a random card;
     - `Buff` at a random card;
     - `Leave`.

     - `Heal` when `hp * PERCENT < run_max_hp * HEAL_BELOW_PERCENT`;
     - `MakeRadiant` at a random card;
     - `Buff` at a random card;
     - `Heal`.
   - `Event { id }`: `Choose` at a random option, then the last option with no negative `hp`, `coins` or `tickets` (as in `walk_tests.rs::free_action`).
   - `Shrine { offers }`: `Bless { Some(random) }`, then `Bless { None }`.
   - `Fight`, `Won` and `Dead`: an `Err`, never `unreachable!`.

     - each `HP entering boss k`, with its mean and n;
     - the rows reached, as a mean and a max, out of `map_rows`;
     - runs won;

## Risks

- **Prototype measurements.** I built a throwaway prototype outside the tree (no marks, 4 cores):
  - At `TINY_BUDGET`, 24 runs across skills 1, 0.5 and 0 were all clean and folded. Each run died within 1 to 4 fights.
  - Seed 0's first 3 fights took 11 s in the test profile.
  - At `AI_BUDGET`, 4 runs took 89 s.
  - With stub fights, runs reached `Won` within 107 steps.
- **Time limits.**
  - If the per-PR test takes over 30 s, set `PR_FIGHTS = 2`.
  - If the daily sweep takes over 10 minutes, lower `DAILY_SEEDS`. It shares a 60-minute job and grows as runs get further.
  - If a fallback happens at the tiny budget, raise `TINY_BUDGET.nodes`.
  - Never use `#[ignore]`, raise a timeout or loosen a clean check.
- **Panics and determinism.**
  - Validate before `create_game`, which panics on a bad setup.
  - No clock, no hooks, a separate policy stream, and results kept in seed order.
- **Replay.** The marks must reach both `play_match` and `fold_args`; the tests catch a miss.
- **Rules 4 and 7.** `crates/ai` gains only a data field, and each AI decides on redacted state.
- **Classify and wire types.** No AI decision changes, so `classify` reads the change as Internal and needs no fragment. `MatchSetup` has no `ts-rs` derive, so `apps/web/src/wire/` is unchanged.
